title: The Problem of Procrastination and Self-Control
coreMove: Turn a distant intention into staged commitments that create consequences before the final deadline.
sourcePressure: The source uses deadlines and commitment devices to show that people often need constraints set in advance to protect long-term goals from present bias.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says use better calendars; the real lesson is that self-control improves when future failure has earlier, visible costs.

exampleSpecs.audience: a facilities director with one annual inspection date
exampleSpecs.stakes: discovering too late that exit lights and door hardware were left until inspection week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director schedules three signed walkthroughs with the fire marshal before the final inspection can become the first real consequence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard hanging from an exit door with a cracked push bar

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer producer coordinating scripts before pledge week
exampleSpecs.stakes: going on air with rushed copy because every draft felt optional until broadcast
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after one failed drive, the producer requires each host to record a thirty-second script test two weeks before pledge week
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a studio clock above a stack of blank pledge scripts

exampleSpecs.audience: a lab manager whose technicians postpone quality checks
exampleSpecs.stakes: shipping crowns late because defects are found only at final polish
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager pins rejection photos beside each interim station and requires sign-off before a case moves down the bench
exampleSpecs.firstImage: porcelain crowns resting in foam slots under a magnifying lamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a legal-aid coordinator managing clients with distant filing deadlines
exampleSpecs.stakes: missing evidence because the real deadline does not create urgency soon enough
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator stamps three colored due dates on the packet cover so each evidence category has an earlier consequence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a manila renewal packet stamped with three colored dates

exampleSpecs.domain: marathon relay team training for a charity race
exampleSpecs.audience: a team captain whose runners keep promising future mileage
exampleSpecs.stakes: arriving undertrained and letting down the charity spot
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain changes the group chat from weekly promises to posted route screenshots every Tuesday and Saturday
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a charity race bib pinned to a cork strip beside blank route slots

exampleSpecs.domain: archive digitization grant with monthly deliverables
exampleSpecs.audience: a curator digitizing fragile letters before a grant report
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing grant renewal because scanning is invisible until the quarter ends
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the curator places a public progress shelf in the reading room where each finished box moves forward every Friday
exampleSpecs.firstImage: acid-free letter boxes lined on a reading-room cart

skillTargets: identify when the final deadline is too distant to shape behavior
design interim commitments with real consequences
separate flexible planning from unprotected intention
evaluate whether a commitment device is visible and binding

tryThisNowSpec: Take one deadline more than a week away and create a public or external checkpoint within forty-eight hours that proves real progress, not just intention.
